samasa.vigraha: mṛduś ca madhyaś cādhimātraś ca; tad-bhāvaḥ

analysis.note: Ablative of cause: “because of the mild/middle/extreme gradation.” The -tva abstract is based on the three grade-terms; Vyāsa applies them to tīvra-saṃvega, intense ardour. Vidyut-prakriya reported a tool_error for this compound-stem derivation and did not supply an alternative; I therefore retain the grammatically regular neuter ablative singular in -tvāt. The dvandva analysis is semantic/exegetical for the base triad; -tva is the abstract-forming suffix, not a separate samāsa-member.

verification.detail: compound stem mṛdu-madhya-adhimātratva as Napumsaka/Panchami/Eka: pass; relation dvandva: unsupported (logged)

analysis.note: Indeclinable ablatival adverb: “from/within that”; here, from the previously stated class of those with intense ardour.
Subject of the verbless sūtra: “a distinction, differentiation”; Vyāsa specifies it as a gradation in the nearness of samādhi-attainment and its fruit.

justifications.decision: Translate the compound as “because [that intense ardour] has mild, middling, and extreme degrees,” rather than as an abstract physical softness/middleness/excessiveness.
options_considered: three degrees of the prior tīvra-saṃvega: mildly intense, middling-intense, extremely intense
justifications.chosen: mṛdu, madhya, and adhimātra are not merely “soft/middle/excessive” in isolation; they mark sub-grades of the already ‘intense’ saṃvega.

evidence.quote: tadviśeṣād api mṛdutīvrasaṃvegasyāsannaḥ tato madhyatīvrasaṃvegasyāsannataraḥ, tasmād adhimātratīvrasaṃvegasyādhimātropāyasyāpy āsannatamaḥ samādhilābhaḥ samādhiphalaṃ ceti.
evidence.translation: “Because of that distinction too, for one whose ardour is mildly intense [samādhi-attainment] is near; for one whose ardour is middling-intense, nearer than that; for one whose ardour is extremely intense and whose means are also extreme, samādhi-attainment and the fruit of samādhi are nearest.”

justifications.decision: Render tato 'pi as “even within that / even there,” not as an unrelated “thereafter also.”
justifications.chosen: tataḥ api refers back to the immediately preceding tīvra-saṃvega class and means that even within that class there is further differentiation.

evidence.quote: tato 'pi viśeṣaḥ. tadviśeṣād api mṛdutīvrasaṃvegasyāsannaḥ tato madhyatīvrasaṃvegasyāsannataraḥ, tasmād adhimātratīvrasaṃvegasyādhimātropāyasyāpy āsannatamaḥ samādhilābhaḥ samādhiphalaṃ ceti.
evidence.translation: “There is a distinction even from/within that. Because of that distinction too, for one whose ardour is mildly intense [attainment] is near; for one whose ardour is middling-intense, nearer than that; from that, for one whose ardour and means are extremely intense, samādhi-attainment and its fruit are nearest.”

justifications.decision: Supply the contextual sense of viśeṣaḥ as a gradation of āsannatā—near, nearer, nearest—in the result.
options_considered: an unspecified distinction of any kind
a distinction in the proximity/speed of samādhi-attainment and its fruit
justifications.chosen: viśeṣaḥ is specifically a distinction in the nearness of samādhi-attainment and its fruit.

evidence.quote: mṛdutīvrasaṃvegasyāsannaḥ tato madhyatīvrasaṃvegasyāsannataraḥ, tasmād adhimātratīvrasaṃvegasyādhimātropāyasyāpy āsannatamaḥ samādhilābhaḥ samādhiphalaṃ ceti.
evidence.translation: “For one whose ardour is mildly intense [samādhi-attainment] is near; for one whose ardour is middling-intense, nearer than that; for one whose ardour is extremely intense and whose means are also extreme, samādhi-attainment and the fruit of samādhi are nearest.”

justifications.decision: Render mṛdumadhyādhimātratvāt as “because of being mild, middling, and extreme / because of the mild-middling-extreme gradation.”
options_considered: ablative as source: “from mildness, middleness, and extremeness”
ablative as cause: “because of the mild/middle/extreme gradation”

translation: Because [that intense ardour] has mild, middling, and extreme degrees, there is a further distinction even within that [in the nearness of samādhi-attainment].
one_shot_delta: A commentary-blind translation might take mṛdu simply as “soft/gentle” and adhimātra as “excessive,” missing that Vyāsa reads all three as sub-degrees of the prior tīvra-saṃvega: mildly intense, middling-intense, and extremely intense.
It might render tato 'pi mechanically as “after that also,” whereas Vyāsa uses it to mark a further distinction even within the class just mentioned.
It might leave viśeṣaḥ as a vague “difference”; Vyāsa specifies the difference as near/nearer/nearest attainment of samādhi and its fruit.
analyzer_disagreements: ByT5 segmented mṛdu/madhya/adhimātra as compound-elements plus tvāt_tva_SBNe; I have consolidated the printed word into one neuter ablative singular abstract stem mṛdu-madhya-adhimātratva. This is not a semantic split of four independent words: -tva forms the abstract noun, and Vyāsa’s line 1 supplies the three grade-members as mṛdu-, madhya-, and adhimātra- applied to tīvra.

Vidyut-prakriya reported a tool_error for deriving mṛdu-madhya-adhimātratva and logged the dvandva relation as unsupported, but gave no contrary derivation; I therefore keep the regular -tva neuter ablative singular and mark the dvandva as an exegetical analysis of the base triad.
